articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5, featuring significantly improved chain-of-thought reasoning, native image and audio generation, and a context window exceeding 1 million tokens. The model demonstrates substantial gains on graduate-level math and science benchmarks, and introduces a new "deep research" mode that can autonomously browse, synthesize, and cite sources across multi-step research tasks.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Agentic Coding Benchmarks
articles.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini Ultra 2, which sets new records on SWE-Bench Verified and HumanEval-Plus, achieving over 72% autonomous issue resolution on real-world GitHub repositories. The model integrates tightly with Google Cloud's Vertex AI platform, offering enterprise-grade tool use, sandboxed code execution, and persistent agent memory for multi-session software engineering workflows.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude's Real-Time Computer Use API for Enterprise Automation
articles.summary: Anthropic expanded Claude's computer use capabilities into a generally available enterprise API, enabling AI agents to interact with desktop applications, browsers, and legacy software systems in real time. Early adopters report 40-60% reductions in manual back-office processing time, with built-in safety layers including human-in-the-loop approval gates and comprehensive audit logging.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in Automotive Assembly Lines
articles.summary: Tesla started deploying its third-generation Optimus humanoid robot in select Gigafactory assembly stations, handling component sorting, bin picking, and quality inspection tasks alongside human workers. The Gen 3 units feature improved dexterous manipulation with 22-DOF hands and on-device vision-language models that allow natural language task instruction and real-time anomaly reporting.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Atlas Commercial Platform for Logistics Warehousing
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics officially launched the commercial Atlas platform purpose-built for warehouse logistics, featuring autonomous pallet manipulation, multi-floor navigation, and fleet coordination through a centralized orchestration layer. The fully electric humanoid can operate continuously for 6+ hours and integrates with existing WMS systems via standard APIs, with pilot deployments beginning at Hyundai and DHL facilities.

articles.title: Figure AI Raises $1.5B Series C as Humanoid Robot Workforce Scales to Multiple BMW Plants
articles.summary: Figure AI closed a massive $1.5 billion Series C round at an $18 billion valuation, fueled by its expanding deployment of Figure 02 robots across BMW's Spartanburg manufacturing complex and two additional European plants. The funding will accelerate development of general-purpose autonomy software that allows robots to learn new manipulation tasks from fewer than 10 demonstrations using foundation model-based imitation learning.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Process Node, Enabling Next-Gen AI Accelerators
articles.summary: TSMC announced volume production on its A14 (1.4nm-class) process technology, delivering approximately 20% performance gains and 30% power efficiency improvements over its N2 node. The process is expected to underpin next-generation AI training and inference chips from Nvidia, AMD, and Apple shipping in early 2027, further tightening the feedback loop between semiconductor advances and AI capability scaling.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Approval to Expand Brain-Computer Interface Trials to 50 Patients
articles.summary: The FDA granted Neuralink approval to expand its PRIME clinical study of the N1 brain-computer interface implant to 50 participants with quadriplegia, following positive safety and efficacy data from its initial cohort. Participants have demonstrated the ability to control cursors, robotic arms, and software interfaces at communication rates exceeding 100 bits per minute, marking a significant milestone toward viable consumer neural interfaces.
